subject: Backup erasure orchestration: ordering, SLA windows, and audit evidence
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@greenbank.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenbank Legal Team <legal@greenbank.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Greenbank request: backup retention timeline and proof of erasure

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the earlier demo — a couple of follow-ups from Legal before we proceed to procurement: we need a clear, customer-facing explanation of how Redwood handles backup retention and how deletion requests propagate to backups and DR copies. Specifically: 

- If Greenbank requests account deletion, what is the end-to-end timeline until data is expunged from all backups (including offsite/DR replicas)?
- How do you show evidence that backups were purged (audit trail/artifacts)?
- Are there scenarios where copies remain after a deletion request (e.g., key destruction, legal hold) and how are those communicated?

I've attached our standard retention questionnaire (Legal_Retention_Request.pdf). We need something we can share with our internal auditors by next week.

Samantha
Samantha Lee
Senior Counsel, Greenbank Financial
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@greenbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 16:38:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Greenbank request: backup retention timeline and proof of erasure

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: we can provide a customer-facing timeline and audit evidence for deletion propagation, with a small set of caveats around legal holds and KMS key lifecycle. Below I mapped the usual stages and the artifacts we produce. Karthik (CC) and Laura (account lead) are looped in so we can produce a single document for your auditors.

High-level stages (typical hosted deployment):
1) Mark for deletion (T0) — customer requests account/data deletion in Console or via API. We create a deletion request record (immutable) and emit an audit event.
2) Logical delete and tombstone (T0 + minutes) — primary dataset is logically deleted; user-facing API calls return 404. We record the tombstone and a deletion token in the audit log.
3) Backup sweep / tombstone propagation (T0 + 24–72 hours) — background jobs reconcile snapshots and mark snapshot fragments for expunge; non-primary replicas are scheduled for purging in waves to keep failover guarantees.
4) Expunge / cryptographic erasure (T0 + 7–30 days) — final expunge runs according to region policy; if applicable, keys for encrypted backups are retired/destroyed which yields cryptographic irrecoverability.

Evidence we can provide: 
- Deletion request record (id, timestamp, requester)
- Audit trail showing tombstone creation and sweep job runs (job ids, timestamps)
- Snapshot manifest updates showing removal of dataset ids
- Expunge job run logs and expunge manifest (filenames, object ids)
- If cryptographic erasure used: key-rotation/destroy event id from KMS (subject to your KMS/contract terms)

Caveats:
- Legal hold / subpoena: we will not expunge data subject to an active legal hold until the hold is released; we provide the hold artifact and expected release path.
- Cross-region replication: propagation windows vary by region pairing; we use a staggered expunge to keep DR restore guarantees (we'll map pair-specific windows for Greenbank).

Next steps: Karthik, can you add the technical ordering and expected timelines per region? Laura — can we schedule a 30-minute call with Greenbank's auditors next Tue to hand this off?

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@greenbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Greenbank request: backup retention timeline and proof of erasure

Samantha / Ben / Laura — technical note from infra side so auditors get the exact sequence. I'm attaching a small diagram (erase-sequence-diagram.png) to illustrate the waves. Key points: 

- T0: Deletion request recorded in control plane (immutable event id: DEL-<unique>). Object metadata flagged as deleted; primary shards are excluded from new writes.
- T0 + 0–1h: Primary tombstone created; immediate visibility in logs and via API. This stops live reads.
- T0 + 24–72h: Snapshot reconciler enumerates snapshots containing the object id. Each snapshot is marked with an expunge candidate flag in the manifest. We intentionally stagger snapshot expunge across region pairs to avoid simultaneous loss of all replicas during ongoing DR drills.
- T0 + 7–30d: Expunge window. For US regional pairs our default is 14 days; EU pairs default 21 days (longer due to cross-region consistency guarantees). Expunge is implemented as object deletion + manifest rewrite. Object deletions are logged and checksummed into the expunge manifest (we can provide SHA256 digests per object id).
- KMS-backed backups: we can take two approaches — immediate key revocation (cryptographic erase) or standard object deletion. Immediate revocation shortens practical recovery to zero but requires KMS coordination and is irreversible; some customers prefer this.

Evidence artifacts we can attach to an audit packet: 
- Control-plane deletion event (DEL-xxxx)
- Snapshot manifest diffs (pre/post)
- Expunge manifest with checksums and timestamps
- Job-run logs with worker ids and latency metrics
- KMS key-change event id (if cryptographic erase chosen)

Open items for Greenbank: 
- Confirm desired expunge policy (standard staggered expunge vs. immediate key revocation)
- Any existing legal holds in scope? If yes, provide hold identifiers so we can map exceptions.

Attachment: erase-sequence-diagram.png (workflow diagram)

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
